risks.note: Opalware is a discretionary purchase. The Company flags that 'A slowdown in economic activity could affect consumer spending and demand for discretionary products, impacting sales and profitability', and separately lists softening discretionary demand and constrained household budgets among its threats — 'Tighter discretionary budgets among consumers and institutions may impact demand for premium tableware.' Mitigation is premiumisation, product innovation and brand strength rather than any demand hedge.

'Increasing competition from organised and unorganised players may exert pressure on market share and margins', and the threats list records 'Increasing participation from organised players is heightening competitive pressures across the market.' The MD confirms new entrants are arriving and that the Company has chosen not to answer them on price, which protects margin but exposes volume and share.
risks.risk: Intensifying competition from organised and unorganised players

risks.note: Overseas revenue is 11.70% of total turnover (BRSR). The Company flags that 'Weak global economic conditions, geopolitical disruptions or trade barriers could affect international demand and export growth', and separately lists 'Export headwinds: Logistics disruptions, container shortages and elevated freight costs'. This is not hypothetical for FY26: the Board's Report (routed to the profile sibling bundle) states that geopolitical tensions, 'particularly the ongoing conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran ... significantly impacted the Company's export operations during the last quarter of the financial year', with disruptions felt across the supply chain. Mitigation is geographic spread across more than 40 countries.

'Volatility in the prices of natural gas, electricity, packaging materials and other key inputs could affect production costs and profitability.' Glass melting is energy-intensive and gas-linked, so this is the primary cost-line exposure; mitigation is operational efficiency, energy optimisation, cost management and prudent procurement, with no hedging or pass-through mechanism disclosed.
risks.risk: Raw material and energy cost volatility

risks.note: 'Evolving consumer tastes and increasing preference for contemporary designs may impact demand for existing product offerings.' The BRSR materiality table frames the same force as an opportunity under Product Development & Innovation — 'Consumer preferences are increasingly shifting towards modern, sustainable and functional products' — making continuous design refresh a standing requirement rather than a choice.
risks.risk: Changing consumer preference and design obsolescence

risks.note: A structural concentration the AR discloses without labelling it a risk: BRSR Section A reports one business activity, 'Table or Kitchen Glassware' (NIC 23105), at 100% of turnover, from three plants only, all domestic (international plants and offices printed '-', a stated zero). Distribution is likewise concentrated — 78% of sales go through dealers and distributors — although top-10 dealer concentration fell to 18% from 21%. There is no second segment, no overseas manufacturing and no subsidiary to diversify outcomes.

'Manufacturing operations involve occupational health and safety risks that could disrupt production and impact employee well-being.' The BRSR materiality table carries it twice — Employee Health and Safety, and Labour practices — noting that incidents 'may result in legal liabilities, insurance claims and employee lawsuits' and that evolving labour regulation is itself a challenge. Mitigation is PPE, periodic health check-ups, safety protocols, audits, preventive maintenance and training. Site-level concentration sharpens this: the BRSR footnote records a suspension of operations at the Madhupur Opal Glass Unit as the cause of elevated FY 2024-25 worker turnover.
risks.risk: Manufacturing health, safety and labour-practice risk

risks.note: The first-listed BRSR material issue: 'GHG Emission posses a significant concern to our business, primarily through regulatory compliance pressures, operational costs, and reputational risks', with financial implications recorded as negative — the cost and effort of establishing more efficient systems to reduce emissions. Mitigation is energy-efficient technology and supplier engagement to align their emissions with the Company's sustainability targets.
risks.risk: GHG emissions and environmental compliance cost

sk.overview: India's gems and jewellery retail industry - covering gold jewellery, studded (diamond/coloured stone) jewellery and other (silver/platinum) jewellery plus gold bars and coins - was estimated at Rs 12,887 billion in fiscal 2026 and forms about 8.3% of India's overall retail market. Demand is culturally anchored in weddings, festivals, births and the harvest season, and gold doubles as a savings asset, particularly in rural India.
